thread.title: After the Bell: Who Cares If the Dow Dropped 7 Points? Apple’s Worth $1 Trillion

author: Ben Levisohn
title: After the Bell: Who Cares If the Dow Dropped 7 Points? Apple’s Worth $1 Trillion
text:
By Ben Levisohn Updated Aug. 2, 2018 6:26 p.m. ET Apple's Day. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dipped slightly on Thursday as the Trump administration said it would consider larger tariffs on Chinese goods . Yet trade was just a sideshow to Apple (AAPL), which won the race to a $1 trillion-plus market valuation . And don't forget tomorrow is jobs Friday. In today's After the Bell , we...
Illustration: Bryan R. Smith/AFP/Getty Images •...observe that tariff threats aren't having much of an impact on the market;
•...wonder how stocks will react to tomorrow's jobs data;
•...and highlight TripAdvisor's (TRIP) tumble to the bottom of the S&P 500 .
What Trade Worries? A day that started off looking like it would end in tears instead ended in cheers as Apple (AAPL) became the first U.S. company with a market value of $1 trillion . Apple's surge helped the Nasdaq Composite gain 1.2% to 7802.69, while the S&P 500 rose 0.5% to 2827.22. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dipped 7.66 points to close at 25,326.16.
Tariffs clearly couldn't compete with Apple, and why should they? The Trump administration is merely using the threats as a negotiating tactic . At least, that's the conventional wisdom. Not everyone is so sanguine, however. UBS economist Seth Carpenter , for one, worries that the "very real possibility of even higher tariff rates serves both to push for a resolution but also to exacerbate the strains," and he doesn't believe that an agreement with China can be reached before the end-of-September deadline.
"This information reinforces our view that the White House will follow through on the imposition of tariffs and raises the risk of escalation beyond our baseline," Carpenter writes.
But the market could have more pressing issues: July's payrolls report is being released tomorrow. The market's reaction to recent jobs reports has been positive, with the S&P 500 gaining 0.7%, 1.1%, and 0.9% on the days of the past three releases. Leuthold Group's Jim Paulsen contends that's because wage gains have been muted but wonders if there's too much complacency heading into tomorrow's report.
Remember, it was a tick up in wages in the February report that helped spur the correction that shaved more than 10% off of the S&P 500. That's some history we'd hate to repeat.
The Hot Stock CF Industries Holdings (CF) shot to the top of the S&P 500 today after its second-quarter earnings beat Wall Street projections.
The shares of were up 12.2%, or $5.37, to $49.50.
CF reported a profit of 63 cents a share, topping forecasts for 45 cents. The company’s revenues were up 15% to $1.3 billion compared to $1.1 billion in the same period last year, and ahead of estimates for $1.22 billion. The company also announced a $500 million share-buyback program through June 2020.
"2Q/18 results were better than expected, primarily due to higher sales volumes driven by catch-up US spring demand," writes RBC analyst Andrew Wong .
CF Industries is up 16.4% year to date and 53.7% for the past year. — Varada Bhat

The Biggest Loser TripAdvisor (TRIP) plummeted to the bottom of the index after disappointing second-quarter results .
The shares plunged 11.2%, or $6.47, to $51.18.
Even though total sales beat analyst expectations, TripAdvisor’s hotel revenues decreased by 4%. The company also reported a 3% decline in its average monthly unique hotel shoppers.
“We believe the market has misinterpreted the results,” says Dan Wasiolek , an analyst at Morningstar . “The shopper decline was due to TripAdvisor's marketing and advertising efficacy effort. We expect the company to see shopper growth in 2019.”
However, Jefferies analyst Brent Thill was less optimistic about the stock. “TripAdvisor remains a transition story with a turnaround that gets constantly pushed further into the future," he says. He maintained his Underweight rating and $31 price target on the stock.
Despite the drop, shares of TripAdvisor are up 48.5% year to date and 35.3% for the past year. — V.B.
